baseline_report.title: Cardiology: Acute Myocardial Ischemia (Inpatient Admission)
baseline_report.text:
PATIENT CLINICAL RECORD - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
PATIENT: Marcus Vance | MRN: PT-2026-8841 | AGE: 58 | GENDER: Male | WARD: Coronary Intensive Care
CHIEF COMPLAINT: Retrosternal chest pressure radiating to the left shoulder, associated with diaphoresis and shortness of breath.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of essential hypertension and hyperlipidemia who presented to the emergency department after experiencing acute sub-sternal chest discomfort radiating to his left jaw and left arm. Onset occurred while climbing stairs, lasting approximately 45 minutes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Blood pressure 158/94 mmHg, heart rate 92 bpm, respiratory rate 20 bpm, SpO2 96% on ambient air. Cardiovascular exam reveals regular rate and rhythm, with an S4 gallop noted. No peripheral edema.
DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP: Electrocardiogram (ECG) demonstrated ST-segment depression of 1.5 mm in leads V4-V6 with T-wave inversions. Serum Cardiac Troponin I was elevated at 1.82 ng/mL (reference < 0.04 ng/mL). Coronary catheterization revealed 85% stenosis of the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery, successfully treated with drug-eluting stent (DES) placement.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: Non-ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI); Coronary Artery Disease.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Aspirin 81 mg oral daily.
2. Ticagrelor (Brilinta) 90 mg oral twice daily.
3. Atorvastatin 80 mg oral once daily at bedtime.
4. Metoprolol Tartrate 25 mg oral twice daily.
5. Sublingual Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg PRN every 5 minutes for acute chest pain (maximum 3 doses).
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS: Strict low-sodium, heart-healthy diet. Avoid strenuous exertion for 2 weeks. Follow up with outpatient cardiology in 10 days. Report immediately to the emergency room for recurrent chest pain, syncope, or severe dyspnea.

latest_report.text:
CARDIOLOGY OUTPATIENT CLINIC - DAY 14 POST-STENT EVALUATION
PATIENT: Marcus Vance | MRN: PT-2026-8841 | AGE: 58 | GENDER: Male
ATTENDING PHYSICIAN: Dr. Sarah Jenkins, MD | DATE OF VISIT: 2026-10-01
INTERVAL HISTORY: Patient returns for scheduled day-14 post-percutaneous coronary intervention (DES stent placement to LAD). He reports complete resolution of retrosternal chest pain and shortness of breath. No angina with walking 30 minutes daily. Adherent to dual antiplatelet therapy.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Alert, well-nourished male in no distress. Blood pressure 122/78 mmHg, resting heart rate 68 bpm regular, SpO2 98% on room air. Cardiac auscultation demonstrates normal S1 and S2 without gallop, rub, or murmurs. Bilateral lungs clear to auscultation.
LABORATORY WORKUP: Serum Cardiac Troponin I has normalized to 0.03 ng/mL (reference < 0.04 ng/mL, down from 1.82 ng/mL). Repeat lipid panel demonstrates excellent response to Atorvastatin 80 mg: Total Cholesterol 142 mg/dL, LDL Cholesterol 78 mg/dL (was 154 mg/dL), Triglycerides 130 mg/dL.
IMPRESSION & PLAN:
1. Post-NSTEMI Status: Remarkable biomarker recovery and complete anginal relief. Stent patent.
2. Dual Antiplatelet Therapy: Continue Aspirin 81 mg daily and Ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily for a minimum of 12 months.
3. Lipid Target Met: Maintain Atorvastatin 80 mg. Patient cleared to begin phase II cardiac rehabilitation.

baseline_report.text:
PATIENT CLINICAL RECORD - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
PATIENT: Robert Vance | MRN: PT-2026-9042 | AGE: 81 | GENDER: Male | WARD: Subacute Geriatric Medicine
CHIEF COMPLAINT: Generalized fatigue, polydipsia, polyuria, and symptomatic morning hyperglycemia.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: An 81-year-old male with long-standing Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus presents with worsening glycemic control. Home fingerstick glucose logs ranged from 240-310 mg/dL over the past 3 weeks. Complains of mild bilateral lower extremity paresthesias.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: BP 138/82 mmHg, HR 74 bpm, BMI 27.4. Monofilament exam demonstrates reduced vibratory and pinprick sensation in bilateral halluces.
DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP: Fasting Plasma Glucose was markedly elevated at 268 mg/dL. Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c) was 10.4% (target < 7.5% for age). Serum Creatinine 1.42 mg/dL with eGFR 51 mL/min/1.73m2. Urine Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (UACR) 180 mg/g (microalbuminuria).
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with Poor Glycemic Control; Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy; Early Diabetic Nephropathy (Stage 3 CKD).
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Empagliflozin (Jardiance) 10 mg oral once daily in the morning.
2. Metformin ER 500 mg oral once daily with dinner.
3. Insulin Glargine (Lantus) 14 units subcutaneously once daily at bedtime.
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS: Strict diabetic carbohydrate-controlled diet. Daily foot inspection for blisters or pressure ulcers. Target fasting blood sugar 100-140 mg/dL. Follow up in outpatient endocrinology in 30 days.

baseline_report.title: Neurology: Acute Ischemic Stroke Evaluation (Emergency Admission)
baseline_report.text:
PATIENT CLINICAL RECORD - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
PATIENT: Eleanor Brooks | MRN: PT-2026-7129 | AGE: 64 | GENDER: Female | WARD: Neurological Intensive Care
CHIEF COMPLAINT: Acute onset of right upper extremity weakness and speech difficulty.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient was in her usual state of health until approximately 08:30 AM when family noticed facial asymmetry, slurred speech, and weakness in her right arm and leg. NIH Stroke Scale score upon presentation was 9.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Alert and oriented x 3. Motor strength: Right upper extremity 3/5, right lower extremity 4/5. Left extremities 5/5. Mild right central facial palsy. Expressive dysphasia with intact comprehension. Blood pressure 172/98 mmHg, heart rate 86 bpm.
DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP: Non-contrast head CT showed no acute intracranial hemorrhage. Brain MRI (DWI) demonstrated restricted diffusion in the left middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory consistent with acute ischemic infarction. Carotid Doppler ultrasound showed 60% stenosis of the left internal carotid artery. Echocardiogram revealed normal ejection fraction without intracardiac thrombus.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: Acute Ischemic Cerebrovascular Accident (Left MCA Territory); Left Carotid Artery Atherosclerosis.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Clopidogrel (Plavix) 75 mg oral daily.
2. Aspirin 81 mg oral daily.
3. Rosuvastatin 40 mg oral daily at bedtime.
4. Lisinopril 10 mg oral daily for blood pressure control.
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS: Home physical therapy and speech therapy 3 times weekly. Strict blood pressure monitoring (target < 130/80 mmHg). Emergent hospital return precautions given for FAST symptoms: Facial droop, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, or sudden loss of balance.

baseline_report.title: Orthopedics: Right Knee Meniscal Tear (Operative Note)
baseline_report.text:
OPERATIVE REPORT & POST-OPERATIVE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
PATIENT: David Miller | MRN: PT-2026-5512 | AGE: 42 | GENDER: Male | WARD: Orthopedic Surgical Care
PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS: Complex tear of the medial meniscus, right knee; mild tricompartmental chondromalacia.
PROCEDURE PERFORMED: Right knee arthroscopy with partial medial meniscectomy and chondroplasty.
OPERATIVE FINDINGS: Diagnostic arthroscopy confirmed an unstable complex tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus. Joint effusion was moderate to severe (Grade 3). Knee flexion restricted to 80 degrees (active ROM 15 to 80 degrees). VAS pain score 7/10.
POSTOPERATIVE COURSE: The patient tolerated the procedure well. Sterile dressings were applied, followed by a compressive Ace wrap. Full weight-bearing as tolerated with crutches for comfort.
POSTOPERATIVE MEDICATIONS:
1. Acetaminophen 650 mg oral every 6 hours PRN mild to moderate pain.
2. Celecoxib (Celebrex) 200 mg oral once daily for 10 days for inflammation.
3. Tramadol 50 mg oral every 6 hours PRN severe breakthrough pain (dispense 12 tablets).
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS: Keep dressings clean and dry for 48 hours. Cryotherapy for 20 minutes every 2 hours. Gentle ankle pumps and quadriceps sets. Suture removal scheduled in 10-14 days.

baseline_report.title: Endocrinology: Type 2 Diabetes with Neuropathy (Initial Consultation)
baseline_report.text:
CLINICAL CONSULTATION & MANAGEMENT SUMMARY
PATIENT: Maria Gonzalez | MRN: PT-2026-4421 | AGE: 51 | GENDER: Female | WARD: Endocrine & Metabolic Care
CHIEF COMPLAINT: Burning dysesthesia in bilateral feet and persistently elevated self-monitored blood glucose levels (220-280 mg/dL).
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: Patient has a 9-year history of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with sub-optimal glycemic control. She reports gradual progression of burning pain and numbness in a stocking-glove distribution over the past 8 months, worse at night. Neuropathy VAS pain score 8/10.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Bilateral foot exam reveals decreased pinprick sensation and loss of 10-gram monofilament sensation in the distal plantar surfaces. Blood pressure 144/88 mmHg.
LABORATORY WORKUP: Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c) 10.4% (markedly elevated). Fasting plasma glucose 236 mg/dL. Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 42 mcg/mg (mild microalbuminuria). Estimated GFR 78 mL/min/1.73m2.
DIAGNOSIS: Poorly Controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy; Early Diabetic Nephropathy.
MEDICATION REGIMEN ADJUSTMENTS:
1. Metformin 1000 mg oral twice daily with meals.
2. Empagliflozin (Jardiance) 10 mg oral once daily in the morning.
3. Basal Insulin Glargine (Lantus) 16 units subcutaneously once daily at bedtime.
4. Gabapentin 300 mg oral once daily at bedtime for neuropathic pain.
PLAN & PREVENTIVE GUIDELINES: Strict self-monitoring of blood glucose twice daily. Daily foot inspection.

DEPARTMENT OF DIAGNOSTIC RADIOLOGY - COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (CT) REPORT
PATIENT: Clara Higgins | ID: PT-2026-9045 | AGE: 67 | GENDER: F
EXAMINATION: CT Chest with Intravenous Contrast
CLINICAL INDICATION: 67-year-old female with persistent productive cough, right-sided pleuritic chest pain, and fever unresponsive to oral amoxicillin.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Temperature 102.4°F, respiratory rate 26 bpm, SpO2 89% on ambient air. White blood cell count elevated at 16.8 x10^3/uL.
FINDINGS:
LUNGS & PLEURA: Dense alveolar consolidation with prominent air bronchograms demonstrated in the posterior segment of the right lower lobe, consistent with dense lobar pneumonia. No cavitary necrosis. Trace right-sided reactive pleural effusion without loculation. Clear left lung parenchyma.
IMPRESSION:
1. Acute right lower lobe lobar consolidation characteristic of dense community-acquired bacterial pneumonia.
2. Associated small reactive right pleural effusion without loculation.
3. Negative for acute pulmonary embolism.

latest_report.title: Pulmonology: Day 10 Post-Antibiotic Clinical & Imaging Resolution
latest_report.text:
PULMONARY CLINICAL MEDICINE - DAY 10 POST-ANTIBIOTIC EVALUATION
PATIENT: Clara Higgins | MRN: PT-2026-9045 | AGE: 67 | GENDER: Female
ATTENDING PULMONOLOGIST: Dr. Elena Rostova, MD | DATE OF VISIT: 2026-10-02
INTERVAL HISTORY: Patient returns for post-treatment follow-up following completion of 10 days of intravenous Ceftriaxone and oral Azithromycin for severe right lower lobe lobar pneumonia. Patient is clinically afebrile for 7 consecutive days (Temperature 98.6°F). Pleuritic chest pain and purulent sputum are completely resolved.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: In no respiratory distress. SpO2 is 97% on ambient air (improved from 89%). Respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute. Chest auscultation reveals clear vesicular breath sounds bilaterally with only minimal trace end-inspiratory crackles at the right lung base.
LABORATORY WORKUP: White Blood Cell count (WBC) has normalized from 16.8 x10^3/uL to 7.2 x10^3/uL (infection cleared).
FOLLOW-UP CHEST RADIOLOGY:
Repeat thoracic imaging confirms near-complete resolution (>90% clearance) of the right lower lobe consolidation. The previous reactive pleural effusion has completely reabsorbed. No new pulmonary infiltrates.
IMPRESSION & PLAN:
1. Complete clinical and radiological resolution of bacterial community-acquired pneumonia.
2. Patient is cleared for resumption of normal daily activities. Inpatient antibiotics successfully completed.
